1.why: All eight screens are static single-column cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up overlays; the only dynamic element is an appended text line in the Logs panel.

2.why: Each step has a large dark-blue heading and one dominant filled blue primary button, though the black 'Logs' console block competes visually for attention with content Helena does not need.

3.why: Each screen presents only one task with a single obvious field and action button, so the needed control is easy to locate, but the technical log area adds irrelevant scanning content.

4.why: Each screen is self-contained, yet the flow requires her to carry a long recovery code and a six-digit code across steps, and the password rule set (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol, no spaces) must be held in mind while typing.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, no autofill hint, no password-manager suggestion, and no show/hide password toggle appears on any screen, including the password creation step.

6.why: Nothing familiar is surfaced — no saved email, no masked account hint, and the password fields are fully obscured dots with no reveal option, so recognition instead of recall is not supported.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain-language, and rendered in high-contrast dark text on white with generous line spacing, although the password guidance and footer notes use a smaller, lighter grey font.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the eight screenshots — there is no invalid-code, mismatched-password, or empty-field message, so the claim cannot be observed to hold.

9.why: The password rules are described in prose but no example string is given; the email field has no placeholder example, and only the code field shows a value because it was pre-filled from the simulated link.

10.why: Two clear alternatives are offered at the start ('Send recovery instructions' vs 'Enter a recovery code manually'), but there is no biometric/face-login or passkey option, and the two grey/blue buttons differ only by colour weight.

11.why: Every screen offers at most two or three buttons and one or two input fields, so choices are never crowded.

12.why: Green confirmation text after sending instructions and the explicit 'Password updated' screen with next-step guidance state outcomes, though intermediate transitions (code verified) are only reflected implicitly by advancing to the next card.

13.why: Helpful hints exist (privacy note under the email field, password requirement line, 'Keep your account safe' panel) but there is no step indicator, no per-step tips, and no help link for new steps.

14.why: Only step 3 has a 'Back' button and step 8 offers 'Start another recovery'; the verification-code and password screens provide no retry, resend, or cancel path visible in the screenshots.

15.why: All screens reuse the identical dark-blue header, white rounded card, same heading colour, same blue primary button style, and the same safety and log panels in fixed positions.
